_doc: Authored dialogue for the arena cast (original writing). Topics appear when their conditions hold, like Gothic's info conditions: cond.has = flags that must be set, cond.not = flags that must not be. once (default true) hides a topic after it was heard. After a topic: set = flags to set, journal = a journal entry, ore = ore the hero gains, effect = 'fight' (this NPC attacks), 'hostile:ID' (another NPC attacks once the talk ends), 'weaken:ID:N' (lower an NPC's strength). Lines are [speaker, text], speaker 'npc' or 'hero'. {ID} in a text becomes that NPC's name. Voices are synthesised per line (tools/voice), named VO_<ID>_<TOPIC>_<NN>.

lines: {KIRGO}. I fight in the pit, when the Barons let me.
Mostly they don't. Today it's {KHARIM} from the New Camp against {GORHANIS} from the swamp. Same as every week.
What's the story with those two?
{KHARIM} fights for ore. {GORHANIS} fights for his Sleeper. Neither has beaten the other in a month.
The whole camp bets on it. {BLOODWYN} keeps the book.

topics.journal: {KIRGO} thinks today's fight is fixed. {BLOODWYN} has bet more ore than he owns on {KHARIM}. {WHISTLER} by the benches may know more.
lines: Is something wrong with today's fight?
Keep your voice down. {BLOODWYN} put more ore on {KHARIM} than he's got.
A man that deep in debt doesn't leave a fight to chance. If anyone knows more, it's {WHISTLER}.
Near the benches. He hears everything, and sells what he hears.
Looks like the fight stays clean.
Thanks to you. Maybe one day they'll let me fight for real.
{GORHANIS} stumbles around like a drunk. Funny thing, that.
Whatever you had to do with it, I didn't see a thing.
Someone who listens. Most people in this camp only talk.
How does the Old Camp work?
The Barons sit in the castle and count ore. The guards collect it. The diggers sweat for it.
The rest of us live in the gaps between. And over all of us hangs the Barrier. Nobody gets out, so everyone wants something else instead.

topics.journal: {WHISTLER}: {BLOODWYN} paid {SNAF} to put swampshade in {GORHANIS}'s stew. I could warn {GORHANIS}, take proof to {THORUS}, or keep quiet and side with {BLOODWYN}.
lines: {KIRGO} says a lot. This time he's right.
{BLOODWYN} paid {SNAF} to cook something special for {GORHANIS}. Swampshade. One bowl, and the templar fights half asleep.
Because {BLOODWYN} owes me ore too. And because whoever you tell decides who wins.
So I heard. You've made an enemy, and a few friends. In this camp that's a fair trade.
Then you picked a side. Remember, I know which one.
Rice and meatbug stew. Best food under the Barrier, as long as you don't ask what's in it.

topics.journal: {SNAF} poured the spiked stew away and admitted that {BLOODWYN} paid him. That is proof enough for {THORUS}.
lines: I know about the bowl you're cooking for {GORHANIS}.
Quiet! {BLOODWYN} paid me twenty ore. Nobody says no to {BLOODWYN}.
Pour it out. I'll make sure he leaves you alone.
You'd better. Fine, it's gone. But if anyone asks, you never heard it from me.

topics.journal: I have the spiked bowl from {SNAF}. Now {GORHANIS} has to eat it.
lines: {BLOODWYN} sent me for the special bowl.
Thought he might. Here. Don't spill it, and whatever you do, don't eat it.
I keep the book. You want to bet, you come to me. You want trouble, you also come to me.
I know what you're planning with the stew.
Do you now. Then you also know there's ore in it.
Fifty nuggets. Fetch the bowl from {SNAF} and see that {GORHANIS} eats it. Nobody gets hurt. Much.

topics.journal: {BLOODWYN} paid me 25 ore to bring {SNAF}'s bowl to {GORHANIS}. Another 25 once the templar has eaten it.
lines: Smart kid. Half now, half when the templar's eaten.
Find someone else for your dirty work.
Careful. In this camp, accidents happen to people who talk.

topics.journal: {BLOODWYN} paid the rest. The fight is fixed, and I helped fix it.
lines: {GORHANIS} ate the stew. Where's the rest of my ore?
Nice work. Here. And this conversation never happened.
You cost me everything, rat. Stay out of my sight.
{GORHANIS}, templar of the Brotherhood. I fight so this camp sees the strength the Sleeper gives.
The one who will free us from the Barrier. Our Gurus see him in their dreams.
You may laugh now. One day the whole valley will hear him wake.

topics.journal: I warned {GORHANIS}. He will fast before the fight, so {BLOODWYN}'s stew won't touch him.
lines: Don't eat anything from the kitchen before you fight.
Poison? So the Old Camp fears an honest fight.
I will fast. The Sleeper rewards discipline. I owe you, stranger.

topics.journal: I gave {GORHANIS} the spiked stew. He'll fight half asleep, {KHARIM} will win, and {BLOODWYN} owes me 25 ore.
lines: Here, a bowl from the kitchen.
Food before a fight is a weakness. But the Sleeper does not forbid it. Thank you.
My head is clear, thanks to you. {KHARIM} will have to beat me honestly.
{KHARIM}, from the New Camp. I come here to beat swamp-smokers and take the Old Camp's ore home.
No Barons, no tribute. We dig our own ore, and our Water Mages mean to blow the Barrier apart with it.
The Old Camp sells its ore to the King for wine and women. We keep ours.
{BLOODWYN} is fixing your fight. He's drugging {GORHANIS}.
What? I don't need an Old Camp rat's help to win!
If the templar goes down, it'll be my mace that does it. Tell {THORUS}. He hates cheats in his arena.
{THORUS}. Captain of the Barons' guard. This arena is mine.
What are the rules of the arena?
Two fighters, weapons out. You fight until one goes down. Nobody dies.
And nobody cheats. Not in my arena.

topics.journal: {THORUS} wants proof before he'll move against one of his own guards. {SNAF} would know.
lines: That's a serious charge against one of my men. Bring me proof, or keep your mouth shut.

topics.journal: I told {THORUS} everything. He paid me 100 ore and will deal with {BLOODWYN}. {BLOODWYN} won't take that quietly.
lines: You've done this camp a service. A hundred ore. And if you ever want to wear the guard's armour for real, come and see me.
{FLETCHER}. Guard. I keep this end of the camp quiet.
That he owes more ore than any man in this camp. Lost it at dice, to the Barons' own men.
A guard that deep in debt gets ideas. Watch him.
How did you end up here?
Same as everyone. The King needs ore for his war with the orcs, so he throws convicts in here to dig it.
The Barrier was meant to keep us in. It keeps everyone else out too. Even the mages who made it.
